chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from al-Alla' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The pregnant woman who is near her delivery and the nursing mother with little milk, there is no blame upon them if they break the fast in the month of Ramadan because they cannot endure the fast. Upon them is that each of them must give charity, one mudd of food for every day she breaks the fast, and upon them is the making up of every day she broke, which she makes up later.'

key_terms.اَلْحَامِلُ اَلْمُقْرِبُ: The pregnant woman near her due date
key_terms.اَلْمُرْضِعُ اَلْقَلِيلَةُ اَللَّبَنِ: The nursing mother with little milk
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A specific measure of food used for charity/expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and compensation for pregnant and nursing women who break their fast in Ramadan due to hardship?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the exemption applies specifically to those whose physical capacity is compromised by pregnancy or lactation, distinguishing this hardship from general illness. It establishes a dual obligation of fidya (one mudd per day) alongside the standard requirement of qada, reflecting the Shia juristic view that these categories face a unique combination of temporary and compensatory duties. This ruling underscores the principle of ease (yusr) in Islamic law, ensuring that religious obligations do not become an undue burden on mothers during critical periods of nourishment.
